posts.name: Vicarian
posts.cooked:
It comes down to cost. Training an AI takes a lot of data, which has indeed been generated for the game on support sites. Problem is that it costs developer time via both active development and research as well as the upfront energy costs (or compute time) to do the training. Because many of your suggested use cases have solutions that actually have been developed (at no cost to Blizzard, mind), it’s not necessarily a great use of money to reinvent the wheel. As far as out of date information goes, it doesn’t take much time to sort comments on Wowhead, say, in chronological descending order and look them over for any updates or changes noted in the same.

If Blizzard doesn’t assert a claim to that information, while the owners of those third-party sites do, then you run into ethics and legal concerns. Which, obviously, is a debate presently ongoing in the space as a whole. I’m of a mind that someone’s intellectual or artistic property shouldn’t be used to train AI unless their permission is sought and explicitly granted.
